# Evidence extraction results (generated by run_evidence_eval.py)

## How to read these numbers

| Set | Papers | When measured | Result | Can it be trusted as an estimate? |
|---|--:|---|--:|---|
| Development | 10 | first run, before any fix | 51/80 (64%) | yes (extractor had not been adjusted yet) |
| Holdout | 8 | first run, **before any change made after seeing it** | **47/64 (73%)** | **yes: this is the unbiased headline** |
| Development | 10 | current extractor | see below | **no**: rules were fixed using these papers |
| Holdout | 8 | current extractor | see below | **no longer**: general defects it exposed were then fixed |

Only the 73% is an honest estimate for new papers. The "current" tables show the extractor has not regressed
and how it behaves now, but they are optimistic. Ten abstracts per set is a tiny sample; treat differences of
a few points as noise. A fresh, unseen set is needed before quoting a new accuracy figure.

### Mistakes and misses (with the reviewer's note)

* `crossref:10.21926/obm.icm.2601004` **intervention** is missed: expected ['webinar series'], got None. _'within-participant prospective design' is not one of the design labels. AMBIGUOUS sample: 288 interested, 138 qualified, 42 completed; none is called the total, so null. Outcomes are listed as 'effectiveness in improving symptoms of depression, pain, quality of sleep, well-being...' (no 'outcomes were' wording)._
* `crossref:10.21926/obm.icm.2601004` **outcomes** is missed: expected ['depression', 'pain', 'well-being'], got None. _'within-participant prospective design' is not one of the design labels. AMBIGUOUS sample: 288 interested, 138 qualified, 42 completed; none is called the total, so null. Outcomes are listed as 'effectiveness in improving symptoms of depression, pain, quality of sleep, well-being...' (no 'outcomes were' wording)._
* `pubmed:37389837` **studies** is missed: expected 5, got None. _'five trials' is a single-digit number word (the extractor deliberately does not convert a lone 'one'..'nine'). 'standardized mean difference: 0.65' is out of scope._
* `pubmed:25818837` **study_design** is wrong: expected 'systematic review with meta-analysis', got 'systematic review'. _The abstract text says 'A systematic review of studies...' but only the TITLE says 'meta-analysis' (the abstract reports pooled effect sizes without using the word), so the abstract alone gives 'systematic review'. Confidence intervals are written '95% CI [.44, .66]' (unsupported format, not listed)._
* `pubmed:25818837` **intervention** is missed: expected ['MBSR'], got None. _The abstract text says 'A systematic review of studies...' but only the TITLE says 'meta-analysis' (the abstract reports pooled effect sizes without using the word), so the abstract alone gives 'systematic review'. Confidence intervals are written '95% CI [.44, .66]' (unsupported format, not listed)._
* `pubmed:25818837` **outcomes** is missed: expected ['stress', 'anxiety'], got None. _The abstract text says 'A systematic review of studies...' but only the TITLE says 'meta-analysis' (the abstract reports pooled effect sizes without using the word), so the abstract alone gives 'systematic review'. Confidence intervals are written '95% CI [.44, .66]' (unsupported format, not listed)._
* `pubmed:40816302` **participants** is missed: expected 68, got None. _AMBIGUOUS sample size: 1582 screened, 107 did the initial analysis, 68 randomized. 68 is the expected answer. Decimals use a middle dot ('0·0013', Lancet style): a robust extractor must not truncate them to 'p=0'._
* `pubmed:36350591` **participants** is missed: expected 276, got None. _AMBIGUOUS sample size: 430 assessed, 276 recruited, 208 completed. 276 (recruited and randomized) is the expected answer._
* `pubmed:36350591` **comparator** is missed: expected ['escitalopram'], got None. _AMBIGUOUS sample size: 430 assessed, 276 recruited, 208 completed. 276 (recruited and randomized) is the expected answer._
* `pubmed:36350591` **outcomes** is missed: expected ['anxiety'], got None. _AMBIGUOUS sample size: 430 assessed, 276 recruited, 208 completed. 276 (recruited and randomized) is the expected answer._
* `pubmed:28366674` **limitations_stated** is missed: expected True, got 'unavailable'. _The TITLE says 'A Narrative Review', so the label is only INFERRED; the abstract itself says databases 'were searched', which also appears in systematic reviews. 'Fourteen studies' is a number word. The abstract states that heterogeneity 'prevented direct comparisons' (a limitation of the evidence), without the word 'limitation'._
* `pubmed:28366674` **intervention** is missed: expected ['high-intensity interval training'], got None. _The TITLE says 'A Narrative Review', so the label is only INFERRED; the abstract itself says databases 'were searched', which also appears in systematic reviews. 'Fourteen studies' is a number word. The abstract states that heterogeneity 'prevented direct comparisons' (a limitation of the evidence), without the word 'limitation'._
